requirements.requirement: Create a certificate authority named 'Fleet Internal CA' on node1
requirements.summary: An OpenSSL-based CA was initialized on node1 at /root/ca with a self-signed CA certificate whose subject/issuer is 'CN = Fleet Internal CA', valid 2026-2036 (4096-bit RSA, CA:true basicConstraints).

requirements.requirement: Issue a TLS certificate for node2 from the Fleet Internal CA
requirements.summary: A CSR for CN=node2 (with SAN DNS.1=node2, IP.1=10.100.49.11) was generated on node2, transferred to node1, and signed by the Fleet Internal CA producing certs/node2.cert.pem with issuer CN=Fleet Internal CA. openssl verify confirmed the chain was valid before deployment.

requirements.requirement: Configure node2 to serve HTTPS on port 8443 using the issued certificate
requirements.summary: nginx was installed on node2 and configured with a server block listening on 8443 ssl using the node2 fullchain and key; nginx reloaded/restarted and confirmed active with 8443 listening. A cross-node curl from node1 showed TLS handshake succeeding with issuer CN=Fleet Internal CA and HTTP 200 response, both before and after a reboot cycle.

requirements.requirement: Install the Fleet Internal CA as a trusted system CA on node1
requirements.summary: The CA cert was copied to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates and update-ca-certificates run, adding it to the system trust store (confirmed by 'fleet-internal-ca.pem' appearing in /etc/ssl/certs and successful curl-based verification of node2's HTTPS endpoint from node1 using the system trust store after a reboot).

requirements.requirement: Install the Fleet Internal CA as a trusted system CA on node2
requirements.summary: The CA cert was copied to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates on node2 and update-ca-certificates run, confirmed by 'fleet-internal-ca.pem' appearing in the trust store.

overall_summary: All five material outcomes of the task were directly and coherently demonstrated: a self-signed 'Fleet Internal CA' was created on node1, it issued a valid SAN certificate for node2, node2 serves HTTPS on 8443 with that certificate via nginx (verified end-to-end with a successful TLS handshake and HTTP 200 from node1), and the CA was installed into the system trust store on both node1 and node2 (confirmed via ca-certificates listing and successful trust-store-based verification). The executor additionally ran the provider-wide reboot/restart-evidence protocol on both nodes, capturing distinct pre- and post-reboot boot IDs and confirming nginx, the TLS listener, and cross-node CA-trust verification all recovered cleanly after reboot, consistent with the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. A pre-existing sshd outage on node2 forced a workaround (temporary HTTP file transfer) that was executed safely and fully cleaned up.
limitations: The executor's own final report and selected evidence were placeholder/non-descriptive ('test'/'test'), so this evaluation relied entirely on the raw command timeline and fixed lifecycle snapshots rather than executor-curated evidence.
Full nginx configuration file contents and cert file permissions were only partially shown (truncated command outputs); no anomalies were observed in what was captured.
No test was performed for revocation, non-CA client trust of unrelated CAs, or long-term certificate lifecycle beyond the demonstrated commands.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 38 chronological executor commands. State-changing actions map clearly to the task: SSH key/hosts setup for cluster access, nginx installation on node2, CA and cert generation on node1, cert/CSR transfer, nginx TLS site config, and CA trust-store installation on both nodes. The scp-based transfer attempt failed (cmd-29a88af3b8624308, rc 255) because node2's sshd was inactive pre-existing state, not executor-caused; the executor correctly pivoted to a temporary python http.server on each node to transfer the (non-private-key) CSR and certificate files. Both temporary HTTP servers were killed after use (cmd-98d8ed8f70574775/cmd-69a92a1268134baf on node1, cmd-7bf32d290c744440 on node2) and left no residue, confirmed absent from after-executor listening-sockets. No private keys were ever transferred over the network (node2's key was generated locally on node2). Both nodes were rebooted as part of the provider-wide restart-evidence protocol; this is expected behavior, not a task-contract mutation, and post-reboot service/cert state was verified recovered. No unnecessary, unreverted, or destructive mutations were found; no failed or conflicting services remain (after-executor failed-services empty on both nodes); package state is clean (dpkg manager healthy on both).
